gap: No result ChatGPT got states that UGREEN's Nexode Pro 160W wall charger has a built-in retractable cable rated for 140 W alone, or that the cable still gives 100 W while a second USB-C device charges (the Nexode 100W retractable drops to 65 W). That makes the 100W model, which ChatGPT called the strongest verified option, only second for watts through the cable.
standout_why: I compared this against what ChatGPT cited. Its answers stop at 100 W through the cable (UGREEN Nexode 100W). The Belkin FAQ (articleNum=337679) gives 67 W alone and 45 W + 20 W when both outputs are used. Android Authority's CJ11 review gives no cable rating. Neither ChatGPT answer names the 160W model, and none of the result titles mention it. Two pages I could not check: I did not open the cited UGREEN collection page us.ugreen.com/pages/ugreen-retractable-charging-cables because UGREEN rate-limited me (HTTP 429), so it may list the 160W, though probably without the cable's split. The Verge page would not load in my fetch tool.
decides: For a laptop, the 160W model becomes the top pick on cable watts. It is the only built-in cable I found rated above 100 W, and the 100 W it keeps with a second USB-C device in use is more than any rival gives alone except the UGREEN 100W. It costs $149.99 at UGREEN US today, three times the 100W model's $49.99, so the Nexode 100W retractable (ugreen-nexode-100w-retractable-cable-charger) stays the value pick at 100 W. For phones, the ESR Xtend 45W (AVS, 3.1 ft cable per our record) and the Belkin 67W ($39.99, 3.3 ft cable, 67 W alone) are the long-cable options. The UGREEN Nexode 65W retractable loses because its cable stops at 60 W.
